title: Implement KnowledgeItem schema and provenance model
body:
Define the schema that carries reviewed operational learning: detection, suppression, remediation, control-mapping, and intelligence knowledge. This is the one core schema from #3 that the walking skeleton did not deliver.

Every item must carry where it came from, so an active rule can always be traced back to the alert, incident, document, or analyst that produced it.

Tasks:
- [ ] KnowledgeItem schema with kind, content, and scope of applicability
- [ ] Provenance references (source alert, incident, uploaded document, or analyst)
- [ ] Confidence score and its basis
- [ ] Lifecycle state field (candidate, reviewed, active, rejected, expired, superseded)
- [ ] Version and supersession references
- [ ] Evidence references consistent with the existing evidence vault
- [ ] Repository persistence and audit events for creation

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Every KnowledgeItem resolves to at least one provenance reference
- [ ] A knowledge item with no evidence and no analyst attribution cannot be created
- [ ] The schema covers all six lifecycle states named in the Project Charter

title: Implement the knowledge lifecycle state machine
body:
Implement the candidate to reviewed to active workflow, plus the rejected, expired, and superseded terminal states.

This owns the lifecycle *after* review. The intake-side review queues are already tracked in #35 (external intelligence) and #51 (manual upload); this issue is what those queues hand off to.

Tasks:
- [ ] Define the allowed state transitions and reject everything else
- [ ] Implement promotion from candidate to reviewed to active
- [ ] Implement rejection with a required reason
- [ ] Implement supersession, linking the replacement item
- [ ] Emit a distinct audit event for every transition, with the actor
- [ ] Reuse the workflow runtime rather than a parallel state machine
- [ ] Tests for invalid transitions

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] An item cannot reach active without passing through reviewed
- [ ] Invalid transitions are blocked, not merely discouraged
- [ ] Every transition is attributable to an actor and visible in the audit chain
- [ ] Superseded items remain readable; nothing is destroyed on replacement

title: Enforce the knowledge promotion policy
body:
Charter invariant: AI and external content may create candidates only. Promotion to active knowledge requires validation or explicit human approval. Enforce that in the policy engine rather than by convention.

This matters most for suppression knowledge — an AI-authored suppression rule that activates itself is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.

Tasks:
- [ ] Deny AI-authored and externally sourced items any state above candidate
- [ ] Route promotion through the approval service built in v0.2.4
- [ ] Add stable reason codes for promotion denials, matching the existing reason-code convention
- [ ] Require validation evidence or an approver decision for activation
- [ ] Apply stricter rules to suppression knowledge than to informational knowledge
- [ ] Adversarial tests attempting self-promotion

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] No code path activates AI-generated knowledge without a human decision or a passing validation
- [ ] Suppression knowledge cannot be activated by the agent that proposed it
- [ ] Denials carry a stable reason code and are auditable

title: Implement knowledge TTL, freshness, and versioning
body:
Knowledge decays. A suppression rule that was correct six months ago may now be hiding a real intrusion, so active knowledge must expire rather than persist by default.

Tasks:
- [ ] TTL field with a per-kind default, shortest for suppression
- [ ] Expiry sweep that moves lapsed items out of active
- [ ] Version history with immutable prior versions
- [ ] Freshness signal surfaced with every knowledge lookup
- [ ] Re-review workflow for items approaching expiry
- [ ] Conflict detection when a new item contradicts an active one

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Active knowledge with no TTL cannot be created
- [ ] Expired items stop influencing triage immediately, without being deleted
- [ ] Editing an active item creates a new version rather than mutating it
- [ ] A conflicting candidate is flagged for review instead of silently overwriting

title: Implement the human feedback loop on triage decisions
body:
Let analysts correct the system, and turn those corrections into knowledge candidates rather than losing them in a comment field.

Tasks:
- [ ] Capture agree, disagree, and correction feedback on a triage recommendation
- [ ] Require a reason on disagreement
- [ ] Convert repeated corrections into knowledge candidates with provenance
- [ ] Link feedback to the originating agent run and evidence
- [ ] Expose feedback in the incident detail view planned for v0.2.5
- [ ] Report feedback volume and disagreement rate

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Analyst disagreement is recorded against the specific agent run, not just the incident
- [ ] A correction produces a candidate, never directly active knowledge
- [ ] Feedback is visible in the agent activity timeline

title: Generate detection tuning and suppression suggestions
body:
Use accumulated knowledge and feedback to propose detection tuning: rules that fire too often, groupings that are too broad, and alerts that are consistently dispositioned as benign.

Suggestions are proposals. Nothing here changes detection behavior on its own.

Tasks:
- [ ] Identify high-volume, consistently benign signatures
- [ ] Propose scoped suppression candidates with an explicit expiry
- [ ] Propose grouping-key adjustments where groups are too broad or too narrow
- [ ] Attach the supporting evidence and disposition history to every suggestion
- [ ] Estimate the blast radius of a suggestion before it is reviewed
- [ ] Run suggestions through the replay framework before they can be approved

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Every suggestion carries the evidence that motivated it
- [ ] No suggestion is applied without review, per the promotion policy
- [ ] A suppression suggestion that would have hidden a past confirmed incident is rejected by replay

title: Define the v1.0 end-to-end demo scenario and dataset
body:
The walking skeleton already satisfies the eight Initial Success Criteria in the Project Charter. v1.0 is the full loop: raw alerts through incident, GRC evidence, approved remediation, verification, and a knowledge update.

Define the scenario before building the demo around it, so the demo proves something specific rather than showing whatever happens to work.

Tasks:
- [ ] Choose a scenario that exercises all four modules
- [ ] Build a sanitized multi-source alert dataset (Suricata, Linux auth, and at least one more)
- [ ] Include a deliberate negative case that must not escalate
- [ ] Include a high-risk action that must require a second approver
- [ ] Define the expected outcome at each stage as assertable checks
- [ ] Confirm the dataset passes the public-repository sanitization audit

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] The scenario exercises SOC, GRC, remediation, and knowledge
- [ ] Expected outcomes are written down before implementation
- [ ] No real hostnames, IPs, or credentials appear in the dataset

title: Extend the demo flow through approval and execution
body:
Carry the demo past the point where the walking skeleton stops. Today the flow ends at a policy DENY with APPROVAL_REQUIRED and no executor invoked; v1.0 continues through an approval decision into a real typed executor.

Depends on the approval service (v0.2.4) and the adapters (v0.4).

Tasks:
- [ ] Drive the demo through an approval decision rather than stopping at the deny
- [ ] Demonstrate the risk-tiered routing, including a high-risk plan needing a second approver
- [ ] Execute an approved plan through a typed executor against the lab target
- [ ] Show that the plan hash bound the approval to exactly what executed
- [ ] Show a rejected plan producing no execution

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Nothing executes without a recorded approval bound to the plan hash
- [ ] A plan modified after approval does not execute
- [ ] The demo runs unattended and is reproducible

title: Add verification and rollback to the demo flow
body:
An execution that is not verified is an assumption. The demo must show the outcome being checked and a failed change being reversed.

Depends on the verifier and rollback manager in v0.4.

Tasks:
- [ ] Verify the intended effect after execution, from independent evidence
- [ ] Record the verification result as evidence, not just a log line
- [ ] Demonstrate a deliberate failure that triggers rollback
- [ ] Show the asset returning to its pre-change state
- [ ] Show the audit chain covering execution, verification, and rollback

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] A failed verification triggers rollback without human intervention
- [ ] Rollback is itself verified
- [ ] The full sequence is reconstructable from the audit chain alone

title: Close the loop by feeding demo outcomes back as knowledge
body:
The last step of the demo is the one that makes it a loop rather than a pipeline: the outcome becomes reviewed knowledge that changes how the next alert is handled.

Tasks:
- [ ] Produce a knowledge candidate from the resolved incident
- [ ] Route it through review and promotion, per the v0.5 policy
- [ ] Re-run the same alert and show the changed handling
- [ ] Show the provenance chain from active knowledge back to the original alert
- [ ] Show that the promotion required a human decision

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] The second run differs from the first only because of promoted knowledge
- [ ] The knowledge item traces back to the incident that produced it
- [ ] No knowledge is activated by the system on its own

title: Add the end-to-end demo acceptance checks to CI
body:
The existing CI runs the tests and a demo smoke check. v1.0 needs the full scenario asserted in CI, so a regression in any module fails the build rather than surfacing during a walkthrough.

Tasks:
- [ ] Assert every stage outcome defined in the demo scenario issue
- [ ] Assert the negative case does not escalate
- [ ] Assert nothing executes without approval
- [ ] Assert the audit chain verifies and replay reproduces the run
- [ ] Keep the runtime short enough for every pull request
- [ ] Publish the demo report as a build artifact

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] The full demo runs in CI on every pull request
- [ ] A broken stage fails the build with a message naming the stage
- [ ] The report is readable without running the demo locally
